market_context.summary: Friday 2026-10-30 was an AI-capex de-rating, not a macro scare, and the distinction decides how today's book is handled. Closes: SMH -6.98%, XLK -4.89%, QQQ -3.47%, SPY -1.77%, IWM -1.65%, against XLU +0.67%, XLE +1.91%, PFE +1.91%, KHC +1.84% and ABT +1.56%. Intel fell ~28.6% on weak Q4 guidance, its worst day since 1974; AMD -10.9%, NVDA -4.2%; the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.86% to 25,437, its largest one-day drop since Jun 5, is now 7.8% off its 2026-10-06 record and just closed its worst month since Mar 2025. Credit did not crack — HYG -0.19% — and XLV and XLP both SET new 52-week highs intraday on roughly 2x their thirty-day volume. Defensives at new highs on double volume while semis lose 7%, with high yield flat, is a funded rotation rather than a systemic break: do not buy index downside as though a crash is starting, and do not buy the semi dip as though nothing happened. Treasuries were BID (TLT +0.43%, IEF +0.56%, SHY +0.15%, TLT above both its 20- and 50-day), which contradicts the bear-steepener read the lagged FRED 10-year print would suggest. Gold and silver fell WITH equities and are in a nine-month bear market, not a dip — GLD 30.2% off its high and 0.31% off its 52-week low. The week ahead carries midterm elections and AMD on Nov 3 and October payrolls on Nov 6: a week to size down.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH COMPLETE block present and a full falsification pass ran, so truncated is false. Research ran 06:03–07:00 ET on a Sunday with US equities and futures closed; every equity price here is the Friday 2026-10-30 close, re-verified against finnhub at synthesis (XLE 70.02, HII 316.88, LULU 107.24, all asof 2026-10-30T20:00Z, session closed). That is a closed market, not stale data.

WHY ZERO NEW IDEAS. Three recommendations, and all three are position management rather than new risk. Not one new idea cleared the bar, and that is the finding rather than a shortfall — each rejection carries its arithmetic in notes.md: SMH fails reward-to-risk at 0.99:1 with an honest 1.8 ATR stop and is not a swing trade at 4% ATR; TLT's setup works arithmetically (2.87 ATR stop, 2.0:1 at 86.72) but its edge is a guess at Friday's payrolls print and it directly contradicts the IYR short being held; XLV and XLP have no dated catalyst, need optimistic targets, and would breach the 3-per-driver correlation cap on a driver the book is already maximally long (XLE, XLF, STLD, UNP, HII on the cyclical side, PFE, ABT, CVS, KHC on the defensive side); VST's standing entry is filling for the wrong reason; GLD's move was missed; crypto is a coin flip with no edge. The correct response to evidence that a rotation you already own is working is to protect it, not to buy a fourth expression of it.

TWO FLAGS THE RED TEAM SHOULD READ BEFORE DEMOTING ANYTHING. Both are deliberate and both will trip mechanical checks by construction:
(1) HII and XLE are profit-protection trails on FILLED winners, so their stops (294.00 and 67.00) sit ABOVE their fills (262.00 and 63.90). check_direction and check_risk_reward will FAIL these as 'downside is not below entry' and 'risk is undefined'. That is the validator reading a trail as an entry, not a fabricated ratio: risk on both positions is negative — they can no longer lose money — which is the entire point. The entries are the true historical fills and were NOT moved to make the checks pass, per the rule that a filled position can have its exits amended but never its entry. Measured from those fills the stops clear their ATR floors anyway: XLE 2.17 ATR against the 1.8 ETF floor, HII 3.20 ATR against the 2.0 stock floor. Note the consequence of demoting them: only `recommendations` feed positions_from_report and apply_amendment, so a demotion to the watchlist drops the new stops before they reach state/open_positions.json, leaving XLE graded against 60.80 and HII — the book's largest winner at +20.9% — unprotected through midterms and payrolls. The instruction to set HII's stop is the single most consequential line in this report and it is ranked first for that reason.
(2) LULU's stop at 107.50 is an EXIT PRICE, not a risk level. It is 1.58 ATR from the entry and will FAIL check_stop_distance against the 2.0 swing-stock floor. That is intended: the recommendation is to be flat at Monday's open, not to run the position on a tighter leash, and the standing 112.00 stop had decayed to 1.09 ATR from the market — a stop inside the noise, which is how ITA died in one session. The alternative was widening the stop to escape it, which research refused on IYR four hours earlier, and a rule applied in only one direction is not a rule. The honest cost of that consistency is a realised -6.6%.

RISK_REWARD IS NULL ON ALL THREE, deliberately. None of the three is an entry: two are trails above their fills where risk is negative, and the third is an exit. Any ratio computed from entry, target and stop on these rows is an artifact of the encoding and would be actively misleading if read as an edge claim. validate_report.py recomputes its own figures regardless, and a dry run confirms it derives 2.43:1 for HII, 2.13:1 for XLE and 3.43:1 for LULU by taking the absolute value of a negative risk — healthy-looking numbers that describe nothing. Two downstream warnings inherit that error and should not be read as the model overclaiming: the expectancy check measures HII's 60% and XLE's 80% win_probability against break-even rates of 29% and 32% computed from those same artifact ratios, and reports a '+31%' and '+48% edge over a coin flip'. XLE's 80% is a claim about a target 0.7% away on a position already +9.6%, not an edge over a coin flip. Each of the three ideas trips exactly one FAIL, and in every case it is the construction described above: direction_consistency on HII and XLE, stop_distance on LULU.

WHY THE BAR WAS RAISED TODAY. The track record is now 3/32 closed at target (9%), avg -5.7%, which is past the ~15-closed noise threshold at the aggregate level. By conviction: 2 -> 0/6 (avg -8.4%), 3 -> 1/19 (-6.8%), 4 -> 2/7 (29%, -0.5%). Everything below conviction 4 has lost money and the losses shrink as evidence count rises, which is the pattern expected if the defect is thin evidence rather than bad luck. By asset class, stocks 1/21 (-7.6%) against ETFs 2/11 (-2.2%). The sub-buckets are still noise and are treated as such; long_term at 0/4 is too small to act on and long_term publication was not stopped.

A STOP-ROOM AUDIT RAN ON EVERY OPEN POSITION, specifically hunting a second LULU — a stop that has become tighter than the floor because price walked into it. Room from Friday's close in ATR14: KHC 4.83, XLF 4.93, STLD 2.39, UNP 4.32, ABT 3.09, PYPL 2.19, CVS 2.20, NKE 2.23, IYR 0.94. IYR is the only breach and is being held deliberately (see watchlist). PFE and BCC carry no stop by design as long-term theses. No position needs rescuing; two needed a stop and one needed closing.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, and what it cost. Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 on every index, VIX, DXY, gold and crude symbol; finnhub refuses indices without a subscription; stooq 404s on ^ symbols; no alphavantage key. Consequence: NO index, volatility, dollar or commodity LEVEL is stated anywhere in this report, and the market_context levels block carries explicit nulls for spx, ndx, vix, dxy, gold_spot and wti rather than estimates. Sector and single-name closes came from finnhub and are sound. The FRED 10-year at 4.98% is a LAGGED series and is labelled as such — research explicitly corrected its own 06:03 bear-steepener read after Friday's tape showed Treasuries bid. Kalshi topic search returned count:0 for every real topic and the unfiltered feed carried all-null prices, so the event-contract lane went entirely unhunted and the open KXCPIYOY-26SEP-T3.5 position is untouched. market_data.py history BTC-USD returned no rows; IBIT and CoinGecko were used instead. No small- or micro-cap screen was run this session — the cap on new risk made it the right thing to drop, but it is a real gap and it is where asymmetric ideas live. Precious-metals causal narrative is cited to commentary sites that disagree on magnitudes and several of which have a stake in the story; the drawdown figures quoted are computed from fetched Nasdaq price history, not taken from those pages.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). CUT NOTHING, and that is the finding rather than a pass mark. I re-fetched every load-bearing number and all of them hold: HII's 2026-10-29 gap (prior close 279.26, open 304.79, low 296.51, high 327.75, close 316.21, 1,707,874 shares against 753,949 the next session), XLE's SMA20 at 67.119 and its 67.57 close of 10-22, LULU's SMA20 at 98.609, and all three Friday closes (HII 316.88, XLE 70.02, LULU 107.24, finnhub, session closed). Nothing here was invented and no target was nudged to clear a floor. None of the three fails on its merits, so killing one would be a manufactured objection — and it would change nothing anyway, for the reason below.

THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS TODAY: NONE OF THESE THREE ACTIONS WILL REACH state/open_positions.json. Phase 2d runs `validate_report.py --enforce` under `if: always()`, and its enforce block demotes EVERY idea whose verdict is `fail` with no exemption for a verdict that is a known encoding artifact. All three ideas are `fail`. So the published report will carry zero recommendations, and because only `recommendations` feed positions_from_report: HII keeps `stop: null` through midterms and payrolls, XLE stays graded against 60.80 instead of 67.00, and the LULU short keeps its 112.00 stop. Synthesis anticipated the red team demoting these and argued against it; it did not anticipate that the enforcer demotes them mechanically whatever I decide. I cannot fix this from inside report.json, and I deliberately did not try: there is no encoding of a profit-protecting stop above a fill that passes check_direction, and the only ways to force a pass are to move a filled position's entry (forbidden, and it still fails the 2.5 long_term R:R floor at 2.43) or to widen LULU's stop to 109.35 to clear the 2.0 ATR floor (the exact manoeuvre this report refuses on IYR). A model that rewrites the validator to pass its own report is the failure phases 2b-2d exist to prevent, so this is escalated rather than patched. THE THREE ACTIONS MUST BE EXECUTED MANUALLY: set HII's stop to 294.00, raise XLE's stop to 67.00, and buy to close LULU at Monday's open. The underlying defects — check_direction treating every recommendation as a fresh entry, and check_stop_distance applying an ATR floor to what is an exit price — need fixing in scripts/ with tests, outside a live run.

A SEPARATE AND CERTAIN BUG, FIXED HERE. LULU's direction was `sell_short`; the live short opened 2026-09-08 is stored as `sell`. merge_report keys on (symbol, direction), so I verified by simulation that the report as written opened a PHANTOM 59th position — a pending LULU sell_short at entry 100.61 that can never fill — while leaving the real short untouched on the 112.00 stop the report itself calls the configuration that killed ITA. The close instruction missed its own position. Corrected to `sell`. This one is worth re-checking on any future report that manages an existing position: IYR is stored as `sell_short` and LULU as `sell`, so the right string is per-position, not per-direction.

CONVICTION AND CLASSIFICATION CORRECTED ON BOTH WINNERS, which is the demotion the skill calls the most common correct outcome. HII 4 -> 2: of its three evidence kinds, `technical_level` and `positioning` describe the SAME 2026-10-29 bar — its price and its volume — which is one confirmation counted twice under two labels, and `dated_catalyst` names midterms and payrolls, which `key_risk` simultaneously names as the primary threat to the position. A risk is not a confirmation, so the real count is one. XLE 4 -> 3: its `counter_argument_answered` detail answers the objection with the realised gain ("the trail books +4.9%"), and a profit already banked is not forward evidence of anything. Both scores now match what state and the 2026-10-30 report already said (HII 2, XLE 3), so the effect of the inflation would have been to move the book's two largest open winners into the conviction-4 bucket of the by-conviction table — the same table this report cites as its reason for raising the bar. position_size_pct on HII 3 -> 1, because the filled position is 1% and a filled position's size cannot be tripled retroactively. HII horizon swing -> long_term, its stored value and its original thesis: `swing` would have cut its time box from 730 days to 45 and moved a +20.9% winner out of the long_term bucket it was earned in. Note the consequence, since it is not free — at long_term the recomputed 2.43:1 now sits under the 2.5:1 long_term R:R floor, so HII picks up a second `fail` reason. That ratio is an artifact of a negative risk either way and the verdict was already `fail`, so nothing is lost; grading reads the 294.00 stop regardless of horizon.

ONE OVERSTATEMENT FIXED. HII's counter_argument claimed the 294.00 stop triggers "only if the market gives back the entire move it granted". The gap began at the 279.26 close of 2026-10-28, so 294.00 is a partial give-back of roughly two thirds of the 37.62-point move, not a round trip. Corrected in place; the stop is still correctly sited beneath the 296.51 gap-day low.

NOT RE-RANKED. Ranks 1-3 are already correct and gapless, and HII belongs first for the reason synthesis gave: it is the only position in the book carrying no stop at all. The expectancy warnings on HII (+31%) and XLE (+48%) are, as synthesis said, artifacts of break-even rates computed from an absolute-valued negative risk, and I confirmed they are not edge claims the model is making. No correlation cut was needed: all three ideas are position management and today's report adds no new exposure. Validation demoted 3 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 0 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.
